sources.title: The Cousteau Society's own account of the Aqua-Lung invention and the Antarctic expeditions
"Explorer, Eco-Warrior, Spy: The Battles of Jacques Cousteau" -- independent journalism

resourcefulness.rationale: During WWII fuel shortages, adapted engineer Emile Gagnan's cooking-gas demand regulator for underwater breathing, co-inventing the Aqua-Lung in the winter of 1942-43 -- a specific, dated instance of repurposing an unrelated existing technology under real wartime material constraint.

curiosity.rationale: In his own words, described testing the new Aqua-Lung with loops, somersaults, and barrel rolls, standing upside down on one finger -- a specific, self-described exploratory, experimental first use of his own invention.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Led the Calypso through a 1972-73 Antarctic expedition during which the ship was struck twice by ice floes in a sudden blizzard (winds rising from 0 to 65 mph in five minutes), holing the hull and breaking a propeller shaft, and during which crew member Michel Laval died in a fall -- a specific, dated expedition undertaken with real, realized physical danger.

adaptability.rationale: Shifted over his career from a naval officer and inventor to a documentary filmmaker and, later, an outspoken environmental advocate after observing pollution and contamination even in Antarctica's ostensibly pristine waters -- a documented change in professional focus driven by his own direct field observations.

impact_motivation.rationale: His own environmental observations from the Antarctic expedition -- finding evidence of insecticides and heavy metals in wildlife in the least-polluted region on Earth -- documented as a direct catalyst for his subsequent conservation advocacy work.

provenance.notes: Roster33 (2026-09-16, docs/checkpoints/roster33.md): building_discovery priority pick (exploration/film). Wikidata QID verified live before scoring. 3 sources: Wikipedia (orientation), the Cousteau Society's own institutional account (primary-adjacent, tracing to his own quoted words on the Aqua-Lung), and independent journalism on his broader career. 5 rows scored from specific dated incidents (the Aqua-Lung's wartime invention, the 1972-73 Antarctic blizzard/ice-floe incident, the pollution observations that catalyzed his conservation turn) -- not from his later television fame or the scale of his filmography (achievement/output, not scored). Crew member Michel Laval's death during the Antarctic expedition was read but not used to infer any trait about Cousteau himself, consistent with this project's health/tragedy discipline (a colleague's death is not personality evidence about the expedition leader). Publication decision (evidence_approved) frozen before eligibility_v2 was computed.
